Brand identity

Where artists and fans meet

Brand identityNovember 2026

Closer to the artists you love.

Egwu is where music artists and their fans meet directly: group chats, live sessions, events, collectibles and rewards, all in one place.

The identity has one job: frame the artist, never compete with them. Soft lilac and deep velvet hold the space so artist photography, product shots and live video can lead.

OverviewEgwu brand identity

Two bells, one handle

The ogene is a double bell that sets the beat in Igbo music and has long been used to call people together. We drew it as one clean silhouette, with no pattern or texture: two voices, the artist and the fans, joined by a single handle.

The handle and the gap between the bells share one centre line, so the symbol feels balanced in an app icon, on a ticket or on a stage screen.

The story is a proposal and needs sign-off. The artwork is traced from the supplied logo.

SymbolEgwu brand identity

Always lowercase in the logo. In running text, write Egwu.

Set in Agbalumo, then refined into custom outlines so the mark can be protected.

The g and w stay close together: in Igbo spelling, gw is one sound.

Soft lilac on deep velvet

Lilac is the signature, velvet is the ground, neutrals do most of the work, and artists bring the excitement. We stay clear of electric violet and hot pink, so Egwu never looks like just another streaming app.

One screen, two modes

In light mode, actions use Violet 600 on Pearl. In dark mode they switch to Lilac 400 on Night, a warm aubergine-tinted black rather than pure black, so the artist’s photos stay rich and the interface stays calm.

The artist’s own photography and accent colour sit inside the frame; Egwu’s colours never recolour the artist.

Light and dark modeEgwu brand identity

Status always has three parts

Colour, icon and word together, so a fan can read the state at a glance in a busy chat, on a slow phone or at a dark venue door, and colour-blind fans never miss it.

Interface typefaceEgwu brand identity

The arch

The ogene’s handle becomes a frame for artist photography: on profiles, share cards and posters. It’s the one shape that says Egwu even when the logo isn’t there.

Graphic deviceEgwu brand identity

Real moments, lilac light

Real people in real moments: the singer mid-song, the crowd with phones up, friends around a record player. Never posed stock smiles.

Light leans lilac. Every photo, stock or AI, is graded toward the palette, so the whole library feels like one shoot.

The artist is the hero. Keep faces clear of navigation and overlays, and never place the Egwu logo over an artist.

PhotographyEgwu brand identity

Rounded line icons

Drawn on a 24 px grid with a 1.75 px stroke and round ends. Filled versions mark the selected tab. Icons that carry meaning always come with a word.

Product marks

Each mark is recognised by its shape, not its colour, and none uses red, amber or green. First concepts for sign-off.

Cowry coinA coin stamped with the arch. Works whatever the coin ends up being called.
Super Fan badgeA rosette that stays readable at 14 px beside a name in chat.
Fan-Club PresidentA calm, arched crest with the ogene. Dignified, not a verification tick.
Proof of authenticityA fine-line seal for collectibles, hard to copy and linked to the item’s record.

Product marksEgwu brand identity

Badge family

Shape tells the kind of badge, dots tell the level. Fans can tell badges apart without relying on colour.

Rewards badgesEgwu brand identity

Proof of authenticity

Every one-of-one piece carries the seal twice: on its listing in the app, and on a physical tag that links back to the item’s record.

Stage-worn, signed and archive pieces are shot like museum objects: one soft light, deep velvet behind, nothing to distract from the piece.

App icon

A Lilac ogene on Velvet: simple enough to spot in a crowded home screen, and different from every music app around it.

Android masks the same artwork into different shapes, so the ogene sits inside the central safe zone.
